question: Under the Medical Termination of Pregnancy (Amendment) Act 2021, up to what gestational age can a registered medical practitioner acting ALONE (without a second practitioner's opinion) terminate a pregnancy for a survivor of rape or sexual assault?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: 12 weeks is the threshold under the original 1971 Act for termination on a single RMP opinion for any indication. The 2021 amendment specifically extended special-category limits further.

20 weeks is the upper limit for termination by a single RMP opinion under the 2021 Act for the general population. However, rape survivors and other special categories have a higher limit under the 2021 amendment.

Correct. The MTP (Amendment) Act 2021 extended the gestational limit for special categories — including rape survivors, minors, and differently-abled women — to 24 weeks with a single RMP opinion. Beyond 24 weeks, a Medical Board decision is required.

answers.text: No upper gestational limit for rape survivors

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: There is no uncapped provision. Beyond 24 weeks for special categories, the case must be referred to a state-level Medical Board, which then assesses substantial fetal abnormality. There is no absolute gestational cap-free category.

overallFeedback.feedback: Memorise the MTP Act 2021 limits: up to 20 weeks — single RMP opinion (general); up to 24 weeks — single RMP for special categories (rape, minor, differently-abled, widow, failed contraception); >24 weeks — Medical Board only.

Correct. The 2021 Amendment raised the limit for special categories (rape survivors, minors, differently-abled, widowed) to 24 weeks on a single RMP opinion. This is the most commonly tested MTP Act fact.
